projects.title: Modern Luxury Villa
projects.description: Full architectural design of a modern luxury villa spanning 3D visualization, interior detailing, and landscape integration. The project required translating conceptual ideas into a photorealistic presentation that stakeholders could evaluate before construction began.
projects.problem: Floor plans and 2D elevations alone were not conveying the spatial experience or material quality of the villa. Stakeholders struggled to visualize the finished result from technical drawings.
projects.solution: Built a complete 3D model in 3ds Max with full interior detailing, material selection, and landscape context. Rendered in Lumion with natural lighting to produce walkthrough-quality visuals that communicated every design decision clearly.
projects.result: Design approved on first presentation. Renders were used directly in the project proposal without revision.
projects.challenges: Balancing architectural accuracy with visual appeal — every material and light source had to match real-world behavior while still looking cinematic.
projects.what_i_learned: How to layer Lumion's lighting system (sun study, sky portals, artificial fill) to create renders that feel inhabited, not staged.

projects.title: Modern Front Elevation Concept
projects.description: Contemporary residential facade design exploring geometric balance, material contrast, and realistic 3D rendering. Multiple elevation options were developed to compare visual impact before committing to a final direction.
projects.problem: A single static elevation drawing couldn't communicate how different materials and massing options would look in real light. Decisions were stalling because each option felt abstract on paper.
projects.solution: Created a detailed 3D exterior model in 3ds Max with interchangeable material swatches and lighting setups. Rendered each option in Lumion under consistent conditions so comparisons were apples-to-apples.
projects.result: The preferred option was selected immediately after the rendered review. No redesign was needed.
key_features: Multiple elevation variants with consistent lighting
projects.challenges: Keeping render times practical while maintaining enough detail for meaningful material comparisons across multiple variants.
projects.what_i_learned: A side-by-side rendered comparison eliminates guesswork faster than any number of markup sessions. The render is the decision tool.

projects.title: Contemporary Villa Elevation Concept
projects.description: Modern residential elevation concept focused on material contrast, lighting realism, and refined facade detailing. The goal was to make high-end design decisions accessible to stakeholders without an architecture background.
projects.problem: Technical elevation drawings required interpretation that not everyone involved in the project could provide. Design discussions kept circling back to basics instead of moving forward.
projects.solution: Produced photorealistic exterior renders from the 3D model emphasizing material quality (limestone, timber cladding, glazing) and natural lighting at different times of day. Used Lumion's atmospheric presets to maintain consistency.
projects.result: Stakeholders could evaluate and approve the design direction directly from the renders. No technical plan reading was necessary.
projects.challenges: Translating subtle architectural concepts — like proportion and rhythm — into a visual language that non-designers could instinctively respond to.
projects.what_i_learned: Photorealism isn't about complexity; it's about getting the fundamentals right: light direction, shadow softness, and material scale.

projects.title: LevelUp
projects.description: A responsive e-commerce frontend for a gaming collectibles store built with React and Tailwind CSS. Features dynamic product listings, real-time filtering, and smooth UI interactions designed to match gaming culture aesthetics.
projects.problem: Existing storefronts in this space felt slow and visually mismatched with the gaming audience. Page loads were heavy, and the browsing experience lacked the energy the products deserved.
projects.solution: Built a component-based React architecture with Tailwind CSS for rapid styling. Implemented client-side filtering and search so users could narrow down products without full-page reloads. Used Vite for fast builds and HMR during development.
projects.result: A performant, responsive UI that loads quickly and feels native. The filtering experience reduced the time to find a specific product significantly compared to the previous approach.
key_features: Real-time product filtering by category and price
Responsive grid layout that adapts from mobile to desktop
Smooth page transitions with skeleton loading states
projects.challenges: Keeping the filter logic responsive while rendering a large product catalog. Debounced inputs and memoized derivations were necessary to avoid jank.
projects.what_i_learned: Client-side filtering with useMemo and proper key management can feel instant even with hundreds of products — the trick is avoiding unnecessary re-renders on every keystroke.

projects.title: Gaming Landing Page
projects.description: An interactive gaming brand landing page with animated sections, responsive layouts, and a bold visual identity. Built with vanilla JavaScript and Bootstrap to deliver immediate impact without framework overhead.
projects.problem: The brand's existing web presence was static and didn't reflect the energy of their gaming identity. Visitors weren't engaging, and the bounce rate reflected the mismatch.
projects.solution: Designed an animated, fully responsive page using HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript with Bootstrap for layout structure. Focused on visual hierarchy — bold hero section, scannable feature grid, and clear call-to-action — all optimized for mobile-first browsing.
projects.result: A high-impact landing page that works consistently across screen sizes. The visual overhaul aligned the online presence with the brand's actual identity.
key_features: CSS-animated hero section with parallax elements
Vanilla JS intersection observer for scroll-triggered animations
projects.challenges: Achieving smooth scroll animations on mid-range mobile devices without dropping frames. Had to throttle intersection observer callbacks and avoid layout thrashing.
projects.what_i_learned: You don't always need a framework. For a single-page marketing site, vanilla JavaScript with a well-structured CSS architecture is faster, lighter, and easier to maintain.

projects.title: Lumo - Movies Platform
projects.description: A modern manga browsing platform with chapter navigation, series filtering, and optimized rendering for a smooth reading experience. Built to address the performance and usability gaps common in existing manga reader sites.
projects.problem: Existing manga platforms suffered from slow load times, cluttered interfaces, and navigation that interrupted reading flow. Pages took noticeable time to render, and filtering by series was cumbersome.
projects.solution: Built a clean React interface with Vite for optimized bundling. Implemented lazy-loaded chapters, a persistent navigation sidebar, and client-side series filtering. Tailwind CSS kept the UI consistent without bloated stylesheets.
projects.result: Page transition times dropped significantly. The reading experience became fluid with preloaded adjacent chapters and minimal UI chrome.
key_features: Responsive grid and list views for browsing
projects.challenges: Managing state across deeply nested navigation (series → chapters → pages) without prop drilling. A focused context structure kept it clean.
projects.what_i_learned: Vite's native ESM dev server and optimized production builds make a real difference in DX and UX. Cold starts are near-instant, and the output is genuinely smaller.

projects.title: Hu Tao Character Poster
projects.description: A character poster inspired by Genshin Impact's Hu Tao, built around dynamic composition, cinematic lighting, and stylized color grading. The goal was to produce a fan piece that sat comfortably beside official promotional material.
projects.problem: Most fan posters in this space relied on simple cutouts and filters. The result rarely matched the polish of official key art. I wanted to push closer to that bar.
projects.solution: Used Photoshop layer blending for depth, light painting to direct focus, and selective color grading to establish mood. Each element — character, background, particle effects — was processed separately before compositing.
projects.result: The piece was well-received across gaming design forums and shared organically. Several commenters mistook it for official artwork.
key_features: Cinematic light painting and rim lighting
Selective color grading for mood separation
Multi-layer compositing with separate element processing
projects.challenges: Matching the character's in-game material properties (hair translucency, fabric texture) using only 2D Photoshop techniques without access to the original 3D assets.
projects.what_i_learned: Light painting in Photoshop — using dodge and burn on separate layers with different opacity brushes — can simulate 3D lighting convincingly when applied with discipline.

projects.title: Jean Character Poster
projects.description: A stylized promotional poster for Genshin Impact's Jean, emphasizing authority and elegance through directional lighting and depth-focused composition. The design centers the character's presence as the Acting Grand Master.
projects.problem: The character's role demanded a visual that communicated leadership and composure. Flat lighting and symmetrical compositions felt too neutral for that personality.
projects.solution: Applied strong directional lighting from the upper-left quadrant to create sculptural shadows across the face and costume. Used depth-of-field simulation to separate Jean from the background, drawing attention to her expression and stance.
projects.result: A clean, high-contrast poster that communicates the character's identity at a glance. The lighting direction reinforces the authoritative tone.
key_features: Mood-appropriate desaturated color palette with selective saturation
projects.challenges: Preventing the strong directional shadow from obscuring costume details that fans would recognize. Had to balance shadow density with detail legibility.
projects.what_i_learned: Light direction isn't just aesthetic — it carries narrative weight. A character lit from above feels authoritative; from below, threatening. That choice communicates before the viewer reads a single word.

projects.title: Deku Motivational Design
projects.description: A typography-driven motivational artwork inspired by My Hero Academia's Deku, where bold type and character art carry equal visual weight. Dramatic shadows and vibrant contrast drive the composition.
projects.problem: Most character posters treat typography as a secondary element placed after the image. I wanted a layout where the message and the character reinforced each other structurally, not decoratively.
projects.solution: Designed the layout around a central typographic lockup, with the character integrated behind and around the text. Used Photoshop layer masks to weave type and image together, with contrasting shadows creating separation.
projects.result: A poster where the motivational text and character presence are inseparable. The typography isn't overlaid — it's built into the composition from the start.
key_features: Typographic lockup as primary compositional element
Layer mask integration between text and character art
High-contrast shadow system for depth separation
projects.challenges: Making the text legible against a busy character background without resorting to a solid text box or thick stroke. Layer masks with feathered edges solved it.
projects.what_i_learned: When type and image share the same visual space, the mask quality determines everything. A hard edge looks like a sticker; a feathered mask with shadow backing looks intentional.

projects.title: Linnea Poster Design
projects.description: Anime-style character poster built around soft lighting, pastel tones, and a calm compositional center. The design emphasizes the character's gentle personality through color and light choices rather than action or drama.
projects.problem: The character reference material was limited to a single illustration with flat lighting. Creating depth and atmosphere from a single source required significant reconstruction of the lighting environment.
projects.solution: Reconstructed the lighting environment in Photoshop using gradient overlays, soft light blending modes, and hand-painted highlight layers. Used a pastel color palette with warm undertones to establish a calm, approachable mood.
projects.result: A cohesive poster that reads as a unified illustration despite being assembled from limited source material. The lighting feels natural and consistent across the frame.
key_features: Reconstructed lighting from flat source material
Pastel color palette with warm toning
Soft gradient overlays for atmospheric depth
projects.challenges: Adding lighting detail to a flat illustration without making the edits obvious. The solution was working entirely with soft light and overlay blending modes at low opacity.
projects.what_i_learned: You can create a convincing lighting environment from a flat source using only Photoshop's built-in blending modes. The key is building up slowly — 5% opacity layers stacked deliberately.

projects.title: Soft Light Cover Design
projects.description: Cover art built around a soft-light aesthetic with gentle color transitions, atmospheric haze, and a dreamlike focal treatment. The goal was to create a cover that felt more like a memory than a photograph.
projects.problem: Standard high-contrast cover treatments felt too aggressive for the mood this piece needed to convey. The subject matter called for subtlety — veiled details, muted highlights, and a restrained palette.
projects.solution: Applied a soft-light layer stack with multiple passes of Gaussian blur, color dodge, and screen blending to create an ethereal glow. Reduced global contrast and let color temperature carry the visual interest instead.
projects.result: A cover that draws viewers in rather than shouting at them. The soft treatment creates curiosity — details reveal themselves the longer you look.
key_features: Soft-light layer stack with Gaussian blur passes
Restrained color palette with temperature-based contrast
Atmospheric haze for depth and mystery
projects.challenges: Keeping the image legible at thumbnail size while maintaining the soft aesthetic. Had to selectively sharpen key focal points (eyes, hair highlights) without breaking the overall softness.
projects.what_i_learned: Contrast isn't just brightness — it's color temperature, saturation, and detail density. A low-contrast image can still pop if you control those other levers deliberately.

projects.title: Kayda Poster Design
projects.description: Anime character poster focused on dramatic rim lighting and cool-toned atmosphere. The composition uses strong backlighting to separate the character from a deep, monochromatic background.
projects.problem: The source artwork had uniform lighting that made the character feel flat against the background. The composition lacked a clear focal hierarchy.
projects.solution: Created a rim light effect by painting highlight layers along the character's silhouette, then adding a deep blue-to-black gradient background for contrast. Used selective blurring on non-focal areas to push depth.
projects.result: The rim lighting gives the character a three-dimensional presence that wasn't in the original. The cool color scheme creates a cohesive, professional mood.
key_features: Hand-painted rim lighting along character silhouette
Selective blur for depth of field simulation
projects.challenges: Painting rim light convincingly requires understanding where real light would hit. Had to study reference images to map highlight placement accurately.
projects.what_i_learned: Rim lighting is one of the most effective ways to add depth to a 2D character. Even a subtle 2px highlight along the edge creates an immediate sense of volume.

projects.title: Bra3am Academy Poster Design
projects.description: Educational poster design for Bra3am Academy blending clean typography with academic visual motifs. The layout prioritizes information hierarchy while maintaining visual engagement.
projects.problem: Academic posters tend to be text-heavy and visually dry. The challenge was to create something that felt scholarly but not boring — approachable without sacrificing professionalism.
projects.solution: Used a clean grid-based layout with clear information zones. Incorporated academic visual motifs (abstract geometric patterns, subtle grid backgrounds) while keeping typography as the primary visual driver. Limited the color palette to navy, white, and accent gold.
projects.result: A poster that communicates academic credibility while remaining visually approachable. The grid structure makes information scannable at a distance.
key_features: Geometric academic motifs as background texture
projects.challenges: Balancing the amount of information against visual breathing room. Every element had to earn its place — if it didn't serve the hierarchy, it was removed.
projects.what_i_learned: In academic design, restraint is the skill. A poster with fewer elements but better spacing always outperforms a dense layout, even with less content.

projects.title: Dr. Poster Design
projects.description: A professional poster design centered on medical and healthcare themes. Clean lines, a controlled palette, and focused typography create a trustworthy visual identity.
projects.problem: Healthcare visuals often fall into two traps: overly clinical (cold, uninviting) or overly warm (losing professional credibility). Finding the middle ground was the brief.
projects.solution: Used a balanced palette of deep blue (trust) and soft white (cleanliness) with selective accent colors for call-to-action elements. Typography was kept simple — a single sans-serif family in varying weights for hierarchy. Clean iconography replaced decorative imagery.
projects.result: A poster that reads as both professional and approachable. The design communicates competence without feeling sterile.
projects.challenges: Designing for a sector where visual trends move slowly. The poster had to feel current without alienating a conservative audience accustomed to traditional medical visuals.
projects.what_i_learned: In regulated industries, clarity beats creativity. A straightforward layout with excellent spacing and typography earns more trust than an adventurous design.

projects.title: Markaz El Kalma Poster Design
projects.description: A poster design for Markaz El Kalma blending anime aesthetics with cultural identity. The composition balances character art with Arabic typographic elements in a modern layout.
projects.problem: Integrating Arabic calligraphy with anime-style artwork without either element dominating or clashing. The two visual languages needed to coexist harmoniously.
projects.solution: Used the character art as the background layer with reduced opacity and a color overlay to unify the palette. Arabic typography was set in a modern Kufi style and positioned as the primary foreground element, creating depth through the layering.
projects.result: A culturally融合 poster where neither element competes. The typography and artwork support each other structurally.
key_features: Arabic typography as primary design element
Color overlay for cross-element visual unity
projects.challenges: Arabic typography has strict anatomical rules (baseline connections, letter shaping) that limit layout flexibility. The design had to work within those constraints, not fight them.
projects.what_i_learned: Arabic script has different optical alignment requirements than Latin script. What looks centered to a Latin-trained eye is often off by several pixels for Arabic. Localized spacing checks are essential.

projects.title: Hu Tao Dark Edition
projects.description: A dark-toned alternative version of the Hu Tao character poster, reworked with dramatic shadows, moodier color grading, and enhanced character focus. A deliberate reimagining rather than a simple filter pass.
projects.problem: The original poster's bright palette, while visually appealing, didn't align with the character's darker personality traits described in the game's lore. The tone felt mismatched.
projects.solution: Reworked the entire color grading pipeline — dropped highlights, deepened shadows, and shifted the midtones toward violet and crimson. Applied localized contrast masking to keep the character's facial features sharp while the environment receded into darkness.
projects.result: The dark edition was preferred by the community over the original for its tonal accuracy to the character. It spread alongside the original as a companion piece.
key_features: Complete color grading regrade (highlights, shadows, midtones)
Localized contrast masking for facial detail retention
Mood-driven palette shift toward violet and crimson
projects.challenges: Darkening the image without losing the detail work from the original (hair strands, fabric folds, particle effects). Had to mask each element separately.
projects.what_i_learned: A global darkness adjustment destroys detail. Selective dodging and burning per element preserves what matters while still achieving the mood shift.

projects.title: Healthy Lifestyle Campaign
projects.description: A marketing poster for a healthy food campaign emphasizing clean visuals, a fresh color palette, and a clear call to action. The design avoids clinical health imagery in favor of warm, appetizing composition.
projects.problem: Health food advertising often falls into either clinical (sterile, unappealing) or indulgent (contradicts the healthy message). The brief required fresh and trustworthy without being either.
projects.solution: Used a light, natural color palette with soft greens and warm whites. The product was photographed with natural window lighting and composited into a minimalist layout. Text was kept to one headline and one call-to-action — nothing more.
projects.result: Design was approved in the first round and used across print and digital campaign materials. The clean approach tested well with the target audience.
key_features: Fresh color palette (soft greens, warm whites)
projects.challenges: Making healthy food look genuinely appetizing rather than virtuous. The lighting and color treatment had to trigger hunger, not just approval.
projects.what_i_learned: In food advertising, the photography quality determines 80% of the result. No amount of layout polish can fix an unappetizing hero image.

projects.title: Automotive Promotional Poster
projects.description: Car-themed promotional artwork with bold studio lighting and strong focal composition designed for advertising use. The vehicle is positioned as the undisputed hero of the frame.
projects.problem: Automotive ads often clutter the frame with environmental context, diluting the product's visual impact. The vehicle needed to be the only thing the viewer saw.
projects.solution: Applied dramatic studio-style lighting against a dark gradient background. Used Photoshop layer work to isolate the vehicle, enhance reflections, and add highlight streaks that guide the eye along the body lines.
projects.result: A print-ready promotional asset where the vehicle commands full attention. The dark background makes the car's form read clearly at any size.
key_features: Dark gradient background for maximum contrast
projects.challenges: Automotive metallic paint is notoriously difficult to composite convincingly. Reflections had to follow the body contours exactly, or the illusion broke immediately.
projects.what_i_learned: Automotive retouching is a discipline of its own. Reflections aren't decorative — they define the materiality. Getting them right means studying how light bends over compound curves.

projects.title: Banking Vector Illustration
projects.description: A minimal vector illustration for financial branding built with clean lines and scalable design principles. The illustration needed to communicate trust and simplicity without relying on stock imagery.
projects.problem: Stock illustrations for financial services all look the same — generic handshake, generic graph, generic building. The brand needed a custom visual that was distinctly theirs.
projects.solution: Created a fully original flat vector illustration in Adobe Illustrator with a restrained geometric style. Used a limited color palette (navy, gold, white) and clean linework. Every shape was built for scalability — the illustration works at favicon size and billboard size without modification.
projects.result: A brand-aligned vector asset usable at any resolution. The illustration was adopted across digital platforms and print collateral.
projects.challenges: Financial services branding is conservative by nature. The illustration had to feel modern and custom without straying too far from what the industry considers appropriate.
projects.what_i_learned: Vector illustration for branding isn't about showing off technical skill — it's about creating a shape language so consistent that it becomes recognizable as the brand's own visual signature.

projects.title: Moon Night Landscape
projects.description: A flat-style nighttime landscape illustration built with layered vector shapes, a limited harmonious palette, and zero gradients or blur effects. The discipline of the constraint drove the aesthetic.
projects.problem: I wanted to explore whether depth and atmosphere could be achieved using only solid vector shapes — no gradient blends, no opacity tricks, no blurs. Most flat illustrations cheat with at least one of these.
projects.solution: Built the scene in Adobe Illustrator using only solid-filled shapes organized into foreground, mid-ground, and sky layers. Depth was created purely through strategic color placement — warm darks in front, cool darks in back, with a moonlit sky using carefully chosen color stops.
projects.result: A calm, atmospheric landscape that demonstrates depth control and color theory working within strict self-imposed constraints. No gradients were harmed.
key_features: Harmonious limited palette with temperature-based depth cues
projects.challenges: Simulating atmospheric perspective (things getting lighter and cooler as they recede) without using opacity or gradient tools. Had to nail each color value by eye.
projects.what_i_learned: Constraints are a design tool. Forcing yourself to work without gradients teaches you more about color value in one project than a year of unrestricted work.

projects.title: Anime Series Cover Art
projects.description: A high-impact anime cover design combining bold typography, vivid color contrast, and modern layout composition. The cover needed to grab attention in a crowded thumbnail feed while still feeling cohesive with the series identity.
projects.problem: Anime covers in this genre tend to follow predictable templates — character center, title top or bottom. Standing out required breaking the template without breaking genre recognition.
projects.solution: Used a bold typographic lockup as the primary visual anchor, with the character integrated as a secondary but complementary element. Applied strong color contrast (warm character against cool background) and kept the composition asymmetrical for visual tension.
projects.result: A cover that reads clearly at thumbnail size and rewards closer inspection. The typography-first approach makes it recognizable even without the character art.
projects.challenges: Cover art must work at two sizes simultaneously: a small thumbnail in a grid and full-size on a product page. What reads at one scale can fail at the other.
projects.what_i_learned: A cover's thumbnail version is the real design problem. If it doesn't work at 150px wide, nobody will click to see it at full size. Design the thumbnail first.
